title: The Effects of Mergers and Acquisitions on Marketing Decisions and Effectiveness: Evidence from the Biopharma Industry
eligible_reason: Main-text models are hierarchical Bayesian pre/post models with an instrumental-variable control function and lagged dependent variable; the only DiD (control drugs) is a robustness check reported only in Web Appendix G, with no estimates in the main text.
design_notes: 375 branded target drugs from 73 M&A deals (2007-2020), IQVIA monthly drug-level data, two years pre and post each deal. Main model: hierarchical Bayesian two-layer model with control-function approach for endogeneity of detailing and price, includes lagged dependent variable and a post-deal indicator, and a first-stage probit residual. Robustness (Discussion section): alternative windows, Arellano-Bond, and two DID models for price and detailing comparing target drugs with drugs in broader therapeutic categories marketed by firms not involved in M&A; specifications and results are in Web Appendix G only. Deal dates differ across drugs so that appendix DiD would be staggered, but it is not a main-text specification under the protocol.
estimators_reported: hierarchical Bayesian regression with IV control function
DiD with control drugs (Web Appendix G only)
screener_notes: Not eligible under the main-text rule. Flag for possible re-screen only if the Web Appendix G DiD is admitted; even then it is likely a matched-style comparison to non-involved drugs with a post indicator and uncertain FE structure. Data: proprietary datasets licensed from IQVIA, Clarivate and MarketLine; stated as not shareable because of licensing. No replication package listed in batch file.
